punchline: A child starting school this year will be mid-career in 2050, in a job market nobody can describe yet.
thirty_sec: Nobody knows what jobs will exist in 2050, Harari says, so a child's memorised facts may be useless by then. He wants schools to teach life skills instead: critical thinking, communication, collaboration and creativity. Above those he puts coping with change and keeping your balance in unfamiliar situations, because people will have to reinvent themselves again and again. He makes the case in 21 Lessons for the 21st Century.
